title: Tshuka Hayim
dek: A traveler whose remembered rules of the Shadow Roads coexist with curiosity, practical aid and a growing place in local memory.
sources: Deep character dossier · supplied 14 October 2026; quest evidence takes precedence
Selected primary scenes and established public histories; anchors below
body:
Tshuka’s account of the Shadow Roads is carried through fear as well as words. Her unfamiliarity with local customs does not make her passive: she observes, asks questions and tries to help people while learning how to live among them.

July 2025 · sound and remembered danger

In the workshop conversation she distinguishes pain from terror: sound frightens her because, on the Roads, she says it can summon a being she calls the Destroyer. Her telepathic voice can remain calm while visible fear spreads across her face.

She says the Roads overlap other realms. These statements are situated testimony, not a complete cosmology. The danger she remembers is real to her, while its identity, reach and applicability away from the Roads remain unconfirmed. Another person’s question about the Wyrm does not establish that the two names identify the same entity.

Curiosity becomes practical aid

Later that day she attends a noisy gathering partly to understand the people around her. She brings drinks, flinches at a microphone and tries to fit in. When she learns of people being held and sold against their will, she reaches out and seeks allies who will help free them.

Her communications with Ryvyt and others preserve concern and coordination under conditions that frighten her. They establish an attempt to help, not a guarantee that every part of her proposed rescue succeeds. Fear does not prevent action, and action does not mean the fear has disappeared.

Belonging and remembrance

The later public funeral record preserves her view that Papirak’s staff should be buried with him or retained for Pristinia’s defense. The alternatives hold memory and civic need together. Her history therefore continues into local responsibility instead of ending with a warning about another realm.

Elenia remains part of her recorded relationship network, but the supplied dossier does not establish a complete account of dependence, mentorship or equality between them. Those possibilities remain questions, not assigned roles.

The open history

Her first arrival, complete relationship history, personal encounters with the Destroyer and the exact mechanisms of the Roads remain unresolved. Her bodily fear supports the significance of the experience without proving every interpretation or requiring a clinical label.

Recorded scenes

Dates refer to transcript postings, not an independently established in-world calendar.

  • 25 July 2025 · her distinction between pain and terror
  • She names the Destroyer
  • Calm communication and visible fear
  • Her realm-overlap account

The skills she can offer immediately

When Tshuka reads Clive’s material list for refugee housing, she realizes she cannot provide those supplies. Her alternative is to conjure temporary towers. She adds blankets, a bathing floor and more space, asking him to move his table so she can continue.

Her help does not depend on pretending she understands the whole political crisis. She keeps asking why the Dasa are fleeing and remains uneasy about inviting people into unfinished arrangements. Even so, she leaves roofs available for anyone without a better option, promises to renew them and returns to do it. Her caution and her practical generosity survive in the same scene.

Keeping temporary shelter available

Tshuka returns to renew the shelter spells rather than leaving them to expire. The later entries explicitly describe repeated maintenance until someone able to build a physical structure can fill the need. This keeps the refuge available through the new source window; it does not make the conjured shelters permanent housing.
